identification.summary: Storm-0501 is a financially motivated threat actor that Microsoft says has been active since at least 2021, when it deployed Sabbath ransomware against US school districts [S2]. It later operated as a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) affiliate using payloads from Hive, BlackCat (ALPHV), Hunters International, LockBit and Embargo [S2]. In 2024 Microsoft documented its expansion from on-premises Active Directory into hybrid cloud (Entra ID) environments [S2], and in August 2025 its shift to cloud-based ransomware that exfiltrates and destroys data in Azure without a conventional encryptor [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: active since at least 2021 (Sabbath ransomware against US school districts) [S2][S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-0501 [S6]. MITRE tracks it as G1053 and states it has been affiliated with Sabbath, Hive, BlackCat, Hunters International, LockBit 3.0 and Embargo [S3]. Microsoft does not date each RaaS affiliation [S2]; the cluster is defined by shared intrusion tradecraft, not by any one ransomware brand. Some third-party profiles equate Storm-0501 with other names (for example Hunters International or UNC2190); these were not confirmed in any cited primary source and are not added as aliases.

attribution.sponsor: Financially motivated criminal actor; no state sponsor is stated in the cited sources [S2][S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft characterizes the actor as financially motivated and tracks it as a distinct cluster [S1][S2]. No government attribution or named individuals appear in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Intelligence telemetry and incident observations in the 2024 and 2025 reports [S1][S2]; MITRE ATT&CK summarizes the group from public reporting [S3]. Secondary coverage repeats Microsoft's findings rather than independently confirming them [S5][S4].

objectives: Financial gain through data theft, extortion and ransomware, and in 2025 through cloud-based extortion that includes destroying data and backups and demanding payment via Microsoft Teams [S1][S2].

targeting.notes: Microsoft names US school districts (2021), the healthcare sector (November 2023 activity noted in the 2025 report), and US government, manufacturing, transportation and law enforcement plus recent hospital targeting in the 2024 report [S1][S2]. The 2025 victim was a large enterprise with multiple subsidiaries, each with its own Active Directory domain and Azure tenant; its sector and region were not stated [S1].

capabilities.summary: Initial access has relied on access brokers Storm-0249 and Storm-0900, stolen credentials, and exploitation of unpatched public-facing servers, including CVE-2022-47966 (Zoho ManageEngine), CVE-2023-4966 (Citrix NetScaler) and CVE-2023-29300 or CVE-2023-38203 (Adobe ColdFusion, unconfirmed which) [S2]. Tooling includes Cobalt Strike Beacon run via rundll32.exe and regsvr32.exe, Impacket SecretsDump, renamed Rclone for exfiltration, AADInternals, obfuscated ADRecon, OSQuery, ossec-win32, and remote management tools Level.io, AnyDesk and NinjaOne [S2]. Embargo ransomware (Rust-based, double extortion) was deployed through a scheduled task named SysUpdate pushed by Group Policy using compromised Domain Admin accounts [S2]. The hybrid pivot involved extracting plaintext Microsoft Entra Connect Sync account credentials, hijacking cloud sessions of Domain Admins holding Global Administrator without MFA, and creating a malicious federated domain with AADInternals to forge SAML tokens and bypass MFA [S2]. In the 2025 case the actor used Evil-WinRM, AzureHound, DCSync, the Directory Synchronization Account to reset a synced Global Administrator's password, attacker-registered MFA, AzCopy exfiltration, then deleted snapshots, restore points, storage accounts and recovery containers, removed resource locks and immutability policies, used Key Vault and encryption scopes to encrypt remaining data and deleted the key, and extorted the victim over Microsoft Teams using a previously compromised user [S1]. Soft-delete limited the impact in that case [S1].

campaigns.name: Sabbath ransomware against US school districts
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports the group first deployed Sabbath ransomware against US school districts, leaked data for extortion and messaged school staff and parents directly [S2][S1].

campaigns.name: Healthcare sector targeting
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's 2025 timeline notes targeting of the healthcare sector in November 2023; details are not given in the sources gathered [S1].

campaigns.name: Embargo ransomware and RaaS affiliate activity
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports Storm-0501 deployed Embargo ransomware via a SysUpdate scheduled task pushed through Group Policy, against US government, manufacturing, transportation, law enforcement and hospital targets [S2][S1].

campaigns.name: Expansion to hybrid cloud environments
campaigns.summary: Microsoft publishes on Storm-0501 pivoting from on-premises Active Directory to Entra ID via Entra Connect Sync credentials and federated-domain backdoors; some cases ended with backdoor access and no ransomware [S2][S5].

campaigns.name: Cloud-based ransomware against multi-tenant enterprise
campaigns.summary: Microsoft describes a campaign in which, after domain administrator compromise, the actor took Global Administrator in Entra ID, exfiltrated Azure Storage data, destroyed backups and demanded ransom via Teams; Microsoft changed Entra ID to block abuse of Directory Synchronization Accounts and released Entra Connect 2.5.3.0 [S1][S4].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated ransomware affiliate cluster tracked by Microsoft as Storm-0501; works with access brokers Storm-0249 and Storm-0900 and RaaS operators [S2].
diamond.capability: Hybrid AD-to-Entra tradecraft (Entra Connect Sync abuse, federated-domain backdoor, DCSync), Cobalt Strike, Impacket, Rclone, AzCopy, Evil-WinRM, AzureHound, Embargo ransomware, and cloud-native data destruction and key-based encryption [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised Entra Connect Sync server used as a pivot with a tunnel; actor-owned Entra ID tenant registered as a trusted federated domain using an attacker-generated root certificate; attacker-controlled exfiltration infrastructure; Microsoft Teams used via a compromised account for extortion. No IPs, domains or hashes are published [S1].
diamond.victim: US education, healthcare, government, manufacturing, transportation and law enforcement organizations, and a large multi-subsidiary enterprise with multiple Azure tenants [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal extortion economy: RaaS affiliate model and initial access brokers; no political motive stated [S2].
diamond.technology: Hybrid identity (Active Directory synced to Microsoft Entra ID), unpatched internet-facing servers, accounts without MFA, over-privileged Global Administrators, partially deployed EDR across tenants, and Azure storage and backup services [S1][S2].

gaps: Initial access vector for the August 2025 campaign is not described in Microsoft's report [S1].
Microsoft does not date each RaaS affiliation (Hive, BlackCat, Hunters International, LockBit, Embargo) [S2].
No IOCs (IPs, domains, hashes) are published in the Microsoft reports opened [S1].
Actor location, identities and any law-enforcement action are not stated in the sources gathered.
Third-party claims of aliases or equivalence (UNC2190, Hunters International, Arcane, Eruption) were seen only on aggregator pages and are unverified.
MITRE ATT&CK G1053 page could not be fetched directly in this session; its description is taken from search-result text and the existing record [S3].
Independent vendor corroboration (non-Microsoft first-party reporting) was not found; secondary articles repeat Microsoft's findings.
No new Storm-0501 campaign reporting after August 2025 was found.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is hybrid identity infrastructure: Entra Connect Sync servers, Directory Synchronization Accounts, Global Administrator accounts and Azure storage, backup and Key Vault resources [S1][S2]. STEP 2: The environment is shaped by gaps such as accounts without MFA, over-privileged synced identities, and tenants not onboarded to endpoint detection [S1]. STEP 3: Threat model: access via brokers, stolen credentials or unpatched edge servers, then Cobalt Strike, credential dumping and DCSync, pivot to Entra ID, federated-domain backdoor, exfiltration, and either Embargo encryption or cloud data and backup destruction with Teams extortion [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued extortion of US public-sector and healthcare-type organizations using cloud-native destruction and hybrid identity abuse. MDCOA is the same tradecraft against a DoD-adjacent contractor or mission-partner cloud tenant, destroying backups and mission data in Azure. Candidate indicators: sign-ins to Directory Synchronization Accounts from untrusted IPs, new federated domains or unexpected federation policy changes, new MFA methods on Global Administrators, mass storage-account or snapshot deletions, removal of resource locks, new Key Vaults and customer-managed keys, scheduled tasks named SysUpdate, and renamed Rclone or AzCopy transfers [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: monitor Entra ID and Azure control-plane logs, not only endpoints, for federation, role and backup-deletion events [S1]. (2) Authorities: cloud tenant administration and incident response for mission-partner and contractor tenants may sit with owners outside the operational chain, so pre-agree who can disable accounts or federation during an incident. (3) Mission assurance: immutable storage, resource locks, Key Vault purge protection and soft-delete are the mitigations Microsoft cites that limited impact; verify they exist for mission-critical cloud data and that backups are logically separated from the administrative identity plane [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators and Microsoft mitigations with DC3, DIB partners and cloud service providers; because this is a criminal actor, coordinate with law enforcement channels as well. Note extortion messages arrived over Teams from a compromised internal account, so out-of-band verification of ransom contacts is needed [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: Storm-0501 is a financially motivated cyber criminal group that uses commodity and open-source tools to conduct ransomware operations. Storm-0501 has been active since 2021 and has previously been affiliated with Sabbath Ransomware and other Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) variants such as Hive, BlackCat, Hunters International, LockBit 3.0, and Embargo ransomware.
